## Acceptance criteria

REQ-01–03 are met. `Strictness::blocks` defines distinct behavior for all three values, and write/transition enforcement applies it at both choke points (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:611`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:920`). Invalid values are rejected during deserialization and `jit config set` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:292`, `crates/jit/src/commands/config.rs:287`).

## Architecture and separation of concerns

No boundary violations found. The pure strictness predicate remains in `validation/`; commands only orchestrate it.

## Functional paradigm

No blocking concern found.

## Correctness and invariants

No atomic-write, event-log, gate, PID-safety, label, assignee, or unsafe-code regression found.

## Safety

No unsafe code introduced.

## Testing

The succeeded `cargo-ci` gate is the primary evidence: 3,586 tests passed with no failures, formatting, or Clippy failures. I did not rerun Cargo tests. New write and transition coverage exercises all levels and invalid configuration (`crates/jit/tests/strictness_enforcement_tests.rs:79`, `crates/jit/tests/strictness_transition_tests.rs:74`).

## Error handling

Invalid strictness values produce contextual errors naming the config key and accepted values (`crates/jit/src/validation/strictness.rs:150`).

## CLI contract

No new command surface was introduced; `jit config set` rejects invalid strictness before persistence.

## Documentation

Configuration reference, templates, and examples consistently describe the implemented semantics (`docs/reference/configuration.md:91`). The prior missing `# Examples` section is resolved (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:361`).

## Prior review feedback

Both prior findings are resolved: eager configuration admission validation and public API examples are present.

## Jit issue management

The prerequisite is done. `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passed; label warnings are allowed.

## Findings

No findings.
